title: Local machine profile and advisors (LOCAL ONLY)
summary: A local-only spec of this machine and its installed apps, and advisors that turn it into proposals you acknowledge one by one; the engine code does the work, these items switch it on.
why: Measured hardware makes tuning and thresholds right for this machine, but it means reading the whole machine, so the module is off until you ask; nothing leaves the machine, and every proposal is backed up and revertable.

items.title: First-run local machine spec ingest
items.does: Reads this machine's spec once: model, CPU cores and threads, RAM size and configured versus rated speed, GPUs, disks and free space, displays, OS build and power plan; saved only in the console data folder.
items.why: Measured hardware feeds thresholds and tuning instead of guesses, for example memory found running below its rated speed. The data stays on this machine: no network, no telemetry, viewable and deletable from the UI, excluded from every export and report.
items.notes: Enable later: when you want suite slots, tasks or app settings tuned to this machine's measured hardware.

items.title: Installed apps and games inventory
items.does: Lists installed apps and games read-only from the uninstall registry keys, Steam library folders and known config locations, with each app's install folder and config files.
items.why: Advisors need to know which config files exist before they can propose anything, and a read-only listing changes nothing on the machine.
items.notes: Enable later: together with the app or game advisors.

items.title: App/game config edit: existing keys only, backup, read back
items.does: Edits an app or game config file only through the engine: existing keys only, never a new key or a changed type, refused while the app runs, a dated backup beside the file, every key read back, and a revert on any mismatch.
items.why: A recorded tuning run worked exactly this way, and one setting the client silently ignored was caught only by the read-back plus a check in the app itself, so you are also asked to confirm the effect.
items.notes: Enable later: when you want an advisor's app or game proposal applied for you instead of by hand.

items.title: Game and app ToS floor
items.does: Never touches a running game process, its memory or its input; only the offline config files the game itself writes from its own options menu are ever edited, and only while it is closed.
items.why: Anti-cheat systems treat process access as cheating, and an account ban cannot be undone; config files the game writes itself are the only safe surface.
items.notes: Always on while the machine-profile module is on; it cannot be switched off inside the module.

items.title: Advisor: machine
items.does: Proposes machine settings from measurements: Temp file count against logon time, free disk, boot trend, RAM configured versus rated speed and the power plan, as maintenance settings with measured thresholds. Every proposal is an ordinary profile change: shown, acknowledged per item, backed up, applied in a transaction, read back and revertable.
items.why: A measured spec is only useful when it turns into changes you approve one by one; nothing is applied without that.
items.notes: Enable later: when logons feel slow or the disk fills, to get measured proposals instead of guesses.

items.title: Advisor: games
items.does: Proposes per-game settings from the GPU, CPU and display (upscaler mode, frame generation, latency mode), applied through the config edit item with the game closed. Every proposal is an ordinary profile change: shown, acknowledged per item, backed up, applied in a transaction, read back and revertable.
items.why: A measured spec is only useful when it turns into changes you approve one by one; nothing is applied without that.
items.notes: Enable later: when you want a game's settings matched to this machine's hardware.

items.title: Advisor: apps
items.does: Proposes app changes that affect the console: startup entries, driver profile backups, browser and editor settings, each with its backup path. Every proposal is an ordinary profile change: shown, acknowledged per item, backed up, applied in a transaction, read back and revertable.
items.why: A measured spec is only useful when it turns into changes you approve one by one; nothing is applied without that.
items.notes: Enable later: when startup apps or editor settings slow the console or the machine.

items.title: Advisor: repo rules
items.does: Proposes suite slots and test workers from RAM and cores, parallel test settings and load-harness limits. Every proposal is an ordinary profile change: shown, acknowledged per item, backed up, applied in a transaction, read back and revertable.
items.why: Suites run in parallel beyond the machine's memory were killed and their partial output looked like results; sizing from the measured spec avoids that. A measured spec is only useful when it turns into changes you approve one by one; nothing is applied without that.
items.notes: Enable later: when test runs compete for memory or cores on this machine.

items.title: Advisor: scheduled tasks
items.does: Proposes a logon-delay ladder without collisions, checks that each task really fires (a Ready state can be stale) and lists trigger expiry dates. Every proposal is an ordinary profile change: shown, acknowledged per item, backed up, applied in a transaction, read back and revertable.
items.why: A measured spec is only useful when it turns into changes you approve one by one; nothing is applied without that.
items.notes: Enable later: once the profile or you have registered several scheduled tasks.

items.title: Advisor: commands
items.does: Proposes which profile commands fit this machine, for example headless lanes only with enough RAM and sandbox tests only where Windows Sandbox is enabled. Every proposal is an ordinary profile change: shown, acknowledged per item, backed up, applied in a transaction, read back and revertable.
items.why: A measured spec is only useful when it turns into changes you approve one by one; nothing is applied without that.
items.notes: Enable later: before turning on headless lanes or sandbox tests on this machine.

items.title: Advisor: cleanliness
items.does: Proposes retentions for Temp, sidecar areas, stale worktrees, runtime folders and Claude transcript size, each from a measured age histogram. Every proposal is an ordinary profile change: shown, acknowledged per item, backed up, applied in a transaction, read back and revertable.
items.why: A measured spec is only useful when it turns into changes you approve one by one; nothing is applied without that.
items.notes: Enable later: when Temp, worktrees or transcripts start to take noticeable space.

items.title: Advisor: professional design
items.does: Proposes console density, font size and motion settings from the display resolution, scaling, refresh rate and the reduced-motion preference. Every proposal is an ordinary profile change: shown, acknowledged per item, backed up, applied in a transaction, read back and revertable.
items.why: A measured spec is only useful when it turns into changes you approve one by one; nothing is applied without that.
items.notes: Enable later: on a high-DPI or very large display, or when the console feels cramped.

items.title: Health findings as rules (generic subset)
items.does: Adds the generic health findings as rules: a Temp count alarm, a cutoff that never fires, tasks with a missing executable (after expanding variables, stripping quotes and resolving bare names on PATH), low disk, a stale backup and orphan headless browsers.
items.why: Findings are rules with measured thresholds; changing a finding's wording never fixes the machine, and a missing-executable check that skips variable expansion reports false alarms.
items.notes: Enable later: together with the maintenance health check, to get its findings as rules.

items.title: Quiet-window benchmark
items.does: Runs benchmarks only in a quiet window: CPU median at most 20 percent and peak at most 25 percent, at night, with background loops paused.
items.why: Background processes changed timings between runs and were mistaken for the effect of a change; a quiet window makes before and after comparable.
items.notes: Enable later: only for projects with performance budgets that compare timings.

items.title: Machine-wide GPU/slot lock
items.does: Serialises GPU or other heavy jobs across repos with one named machine-wide lock and a slot bucket.
items.why: One GPU shared by several loops was oversubscribed, and copies of the lock code that drifted apart silently stopped catching each other.
items.notes: Enable later: only when several repos share one GPU or another heavy device.
